facts.text: MO-Gymnasium follows the Gymnasium API but returns vectorized rewards as numpy arrays
fishwood-v0 is registered with the entry point mo_gymnasium.envs.fishwood.fishwood:FishWood and no max_episode_steps wrapper
The observation space is Box(low=0, high=1, shape=(1,), dtype=int32) and has two states: 0 fishing and 1 in the woods
The action space is Discrete(2): 0 go fishing and 1 go collect wood
The reward is 2-dimensional with one objective per resource
The state constants are FISH 0, WOOD 1 and MAX_TS 200
The constructor defaults fishproba to 0.1 and woodproba to 0.9
The observation space is spaces.Box(low=0, high=1, shape=(1,), dtype=int32)
The reward space is spaces.Box(low=[0, 0], high=[1.0, 1.0], dtype=float32) and reward_dim is 2
The fisherman starts in the woods: _state is WOOD and reset restores that state with timestep 0
reset calls super().reset(seed=seed), so the seed arms the environment's np_random generator
step draws a Bernoulli reward for the state the fisherman is leaving: woodproba pays the wood objective and fishproba pays the fish objective
step sets the state to [action] and increments the timestep
The episode returns terminated and truncated when the timestep equals MAX_TS
The episode ends after MAX_TS = 200 steps
mo_gymnasium.make disables the gymnasium env checker because it requires the reward to be a scalar

determinism.notes: reset(seed) arms the fake's random generator and the transition rule is deterministic, so one seed and one action sequence repeat a trajectory; the fake draws with Python's random.Random while upstream draws from numpy's Generator, so the same seed gives different reward sequences on the two

gaps: no dynamics: the model has two states (fishing 0 and in the woods 1) and one tick applies the action's state and the Bernoulli reward of the state left behind; no forces, contacts or continuous time are modelled (F0)
no simulation time advances: the environment is turn-based, timestep_ms is 0, one tick is one action and realtime_factor 0 means no wall-clock pacing

the 2-objective reward vector of MO-Gymnasium (README.md:13) is not carried by cap.world.step.v1, whose reward is a single number; the fake returns the sum of the one-hot objectives (0 or 1) as the scalar reward and keeps the full [fish, wood] vector in info.objectives, so the vector is absent from the step output

the fake draws the Bernoulli reward with Python's random.Random instead of numpy's np_random and was never compared with an upstream run (MO-Gymnasium needs gymnasium, numpy and pygame-ce, which the gate does not have)
no rendering, no pygame assets, no snapshot/restore (the class exposes no get_state/set_state) and no physical device is modelled; nothing was validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
